To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the incidence of decompression sickness was increased by alimentary lipemia and (ii) the platelet counts were reduced by decompression and by an attack of bends, and that this reduction was accentuated by alimentary lipenia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the production of bends and of the influence upon these of dietary fat, lipemia, and lipemia-clearing agents.
the effects of dietary fat on decompression sickness in the rat.
the effects of aeroembolization and the influence of alimentary lipemia upon blood lipid concentration and blood cell counts in rats.

the results of these studies indicate that alimentary lipaemia increases the incidence of bends, that a lipaemia-clearing agent may reduce the incidence of bends and that platelet aggregation may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of bends.

the use of the lipemia-clearing agents in combination with a high-fat diet can reduce the risk of decompression sickness, but it should be emphasized that the use of these agents should be done in combination with other preventive measures such as the use of recompression chambers and the use of decompression tables.
